column5: GROUP: **isa-aarch64** | - A-SFE:7138, 7432, 7967, 7407, 8004. Hosted `effects`/`size`/`declaration` use the Linux register for any target that is not macOS arm64. Reader: "traced to the gate, gate body open" (`isa-aarch64/src/machine_effects.rs:275-281` read, `aarch64_selected_abi` not). A third AArch64 target would get a Linux clobber declared; `request` would still refuse to encode it.
GROUP: **isa-aarch64** | - A-SFE:4928-4932. System-register access declares more clobbers than its one word writes. Reader: declares more than is written, not an accept risk; reason unknown.

GROUP: **isa-x86_64** | - `machine_effects.rs:1395-1403`. The second `match semantic` in `encoded_effects` has a `_ =>` arm that declares no effects. A newly added semantic with a side effect would be catalogued as effect-free, and the validator rebuilds with the same builder so it would not notice (u008).
GROUP: **isa-x86_64** | - `frame_protocol.rs:390-392`. With `alignment_bytes == 1` the validator never looks at `member_offset_bytes`. Reader did not grep callers.
GROUP: **isa-x86_64** | - `generated_entry.rs:539-541`. Local-call target is computed without a range check here; `from_target_instructions` (not read) "presumably validates".
GROUP: **isa-x86_64** | - `generated_entry.rs:528-542`. A call whose field offset is not `body_call_field` is silently treated as a local call.
GROUP: **isa-x86_64** | - X-SFE:2843-2927. `AtomicAccess` indexes `registers` without a length guard; a short list panics rather than accepts. Caller guarantee unread.
GROUP: **isa-x86_64** | - `post_handoff_writer.rs:118-138`. Byte-loop path for widths other than 1/2/4/8; whether `validate_fragment` allows such widths is in another file, unverified.
